interface_detail: SSH on port 22, plus web hosting
tooling: SSH, cron, a FreeBSD userspace, a web panel
chaining: 3 GB of disk with a shell and cron, behind a non-profit gate
limits_note: resource limits beyond the 3 GB disk are not published on the pricing page

free_tier.stated: 3 GB of SSD storage, unlimited data transfer, support for up to 100 websites and 16 databases; registration is free and reviewed by hand
free_tier.notes: the vendor writes 3 GB, a decimal unit; the figure is kept as stated and not converted to GiB

retention.stated: A user account that has not been properly logged in by the DevilWEB or SSH panel for a period of 90 days will be automatically removed from the system without the possibility of recovering the data collected on that account.
retention.notes: the 90-day clock is reset by a DevilWEB panel login as well as by SSH

egress.terms: unlimited data transfer; the home page states 'unlimited data transfer' with no volume, no shaping tier and no price beyond the allowance

limits.value: 3 GB of SSD storage per account (vendor's decimal GB)
account deleted after 90 days without a DevilWEB or SSH login
a concurrent system-process limit exists; the number is not published, and exceeding it returns 'Server refused to start a shell/command'
a port can be reserved from 1024 to 64000, TCP or UDP, with `devil port add`; the number of reservations per account is not published

identity_cost.detail: email address, first name, last name, one anti-bot question and a reCAPTCHA; the form carries no card field and no phone field. The application is then reviewed by hand: 'Your application has been successfully submitted and is now awaiting manual review. This process usually takes anywhere from a few hours up to 72 hours.' No card, no phone, no document.

'3 GB for free, no adverts, no hooks'

notes: Two caveats that decide the row. First, the account is not instant: the form says a few hours up to 72 hours of manual review, so it cannot be relied on tonight. Second, the home page counter read 167,472 of 170,000 accounts, which is 2,528 slots, so registration may close without notice. RAM and vCPU are not published; do not fill them in from a forum. What would settle them: a probe on an approved account reading `ulimit -a`, `sysctl hw.physmem` and the process ceiling from `procstat`.

session_cap.note: no session cap is published; the published reap is 90 days without a login, and a concurrent-process ceiling can refuse a shell

network_out.ports: one reserved port in 1024-64000 per reservation, TCP or UDP

extras.shape_note: vendor states 3 GB (decimal) of SSD; kept as stated, not converted. No RAM or vCPU figure is published on any page read.
extras.term: indefinite while the account logs in at least once per 90 days
extras.price_arithmetic: no charge; the offer is free

confidence_note: disk, traffic, account count and the review sentence from the vendor's own pages read today; the port range from the docs. RAM and vCPU are not published anywhere read, so they are null rather than guessed.

probe.note: the saved run this record cites, kept in sources/ so it survives a clean tree; re-run it with scripts/probe/tcpprobe.py

binding_note: 3 GB of disk and an unpublished concurrent-process ceiling are hit long before the unlimited traffic term matters; the process ceiling blocks SSH itself, not just the workload.
